messages.text: How does this compare to ATLAS ITK and CMS Phase-2?
I’ll compare the channel counts, sensor segmentation and hit-resolution estimates, using the published ATLAS ITk and CMS Phase-2 designs.

The main difference is the strixel system: it brings our outer-tracker count to about 1.55 billion channels, versus roughly 60 million for ITk and 212 million for CMS. Its 0.5 mm second-coordinate segmentation is much finer than CMS’s roughly 1.5 mm macro-pixels; ITk uses stereo strips to measure that coordinate.

**Our pixel system is close to CMS Phase-2 in channel count. The major difference is our strixel system, which makes the outer tracker much more granular.**

These are **whole-detector totals: barrel plus both endcaps**, rounded for comparison.

| Channels, millions | Our baseline | ATLAS ITk | CMS Phase-2 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Fine pixels | 1,906 | ≈5,000 | ≈2,000 |
| Strixels / macro-pixels | 1,522 | — | ≈170 |
| Conventional strips | 25.7 | ≈60 | ≈42 |
| **Outer tracker subtotal** | **1,547** | **≈60** | **≈212** |
| **Full tracker** | **3,454** | **≈5,060** | **≈2,212** |

The reference counts come from the [ATLAS ITk overview](https://cds.cern.ch/record/2940697/files/ATL-ITK-SLIDE-2025-390.pdf) and [CMS Phase-2 overview]([external URL redacted; see source journal]). Our outer tracker therefore has approximately **26× ITk’s** and **7.3× CMS’s** channel count.

The closest sensor comparisons are:

| Feature | Our baseline | ATLAS ITk | CMS Phase-2 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pixel cells | 50 × 50 µm² | Mostly 50 × 50 µm²; innermost barrel 25 × 100 µm² | 25 × 100 µm² |
| Intermediate sensors | 75 µm × 0.5 mm strixels | Barrel short strips: 75.5 µm pitch, 24.1 mm length | PS macro-pixels: 100 µm × ≈1.47 mm, paired with strip sensors |
| Long strips | 80 µm pitch, 96 mm length | Barrel: 75.5 µm pitch, 48.2 mm length | 2S: 90 µm pitch, ≈50 mm length |

ITk endcaps use varying strip pitches and lengths. Sources: [ITk pixels](https://cds.cern.ch/record/2949152/files/ATL-ITK-PROC-2025-028.pdf?version=1), [ITk strips](https://cds.cern.ch/record/2790149/files/ATL-ITK-SLIDE-2021-689.pdf), [CMS pixels](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.13304), [CMS outer sensors]([external URL redacted; see source journal]).

Using the same **ideal binary resolution** convention as before:

- **Pixels:** our **(14.4, 14.4) µm** matches ITk’s square pixels. CMS’s rectangular pixels give **(7.2, 28.9) µm**, trading precision between coordinates at the same pixel area.
- **Strixels:** our **(21.7, 144) µm** compares with approximately **(28.9, 423) µm** for CMS macro-pixels. Our cells provide **3.9× more channels per unit area**.
- **Strips:** transverse resolution per face is similar: **23.1 µm ours**, **21.8 µm ITk barrel**, **26.0 µm CMS 2S**. Our strips are approximately twice as long.

ITk obtains its second strip coordinate through stereo measurements. CMS’s paired sensors additionally support **on-module momentum discrimination and the Level-1 track trigger**, so their doublets serve a different purpose from our stereo pairs. [CMS doublet design](https://arxiv.org/html/2404.08794v2#S1)

The strongest distinction is therefore **our fine second-coordinate measurement across a large strixel area**, with its corresponding readout-channel burden.
